question: Which language among the following is a Sino-Tibetan language spoken by people of north-east India?
solution:
The correct answer is **'__Bodo__'.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• The Sino-Tibetan is also known as the **Mongoloid Family** and **Bodo** is the type of **SinoTibetan language.**
 
• It **stretches all over the sub-Himalayan tracts up to the north-western frontier** and covers the** Indian states of North Bihar, North Bengal, and Assam.**
 
• These languages are considered to be older than the Indo-Aryan languages and are referred to as Kiratas in the oldest Sanskrit literature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Maithili:**

 
 
• **​**Maithili language, with Magadhi (Magahi) and Bhojpuri, one of the three main** languages of Bihar state**.
 
• It is an** Indo-Aryan language** of the Indo-European language family. 
 
• Maithili is one of India's 22 scheduled languages.
 
 
 
• **Santhali:**
 
 
• **​**Santali language, Santali also spelled Santhali, a** Munda language spoken** primarily in the **east-central Indian states** of West Bengal, Jharkhand, and Orissa. 
 
• Santali is one of India's 22 scheduled languages.
 
 
 
• **Dogri:**
 
 
• **​**Dogri language is spoken in the UT of Jammu & Kashmi, also spoken in some regions of Himachal Pradesh and Punjab.
 
• Dogri is the language of the Dogras, living mainly in the Jammu region of Jammu and Kashmir. 
 
• Dogri language is a **member of the Indo-Aryan** i.e. language of Vedas and Laukik Sanskrit group within the Indo-European languages of India.
 
• Dogri is one of India's 22 scheduled languages
